Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Pair-key provisioning

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Pair_Service is an optional bounded read service over an existing P2P Hub. It supplies the native link with a pair grant and the remote member's currently registered endpoint. It does not alter durable schemas or grant simulation authority. Embeddings route its messages explicitly; the Duel service now enables it alongside provisioning, registration and RTC signaling.

Requests/replies use separate canonical kinds 0x5054 / 0x5055, version 1 and separate HMAC domains. A request binds room/content, current identity, the process registration nonce, remote member and a fresh challenge. The service checks the MAC, current enabled identity and exact registered nonce before deriving a key. Only full fixed rosters with a registered remote member are eligible. Reply errors carry no key or endpoint.

The service rate-limits each enrolled member independently (burst 8, four reads per second), does not write storage, and refuses poisoned owners or backwards time. Pair secrets are deterministic for their committed scope/identities. A remote rebind changes the returned key; an old requester incarnation is denied.

Use the same verified confidential transport as enrollment. A MAC is not encryption. Only explicit loopback fixtures may use a plain channel. Never place pair replies in public rosters, recordings or participant archives.

Pair_Client borrows a ready registration Client, clock and transport. Route its packets separately from registration RPCs (a Router lane is suitable). Each begin requires a new nonzero challenge; adjacent reuse is refused. Replies must match the exact signed request hash, member pair and the owner's accepted match scope. The client retries within a ten-second bound. Close it before its borrowed owner.

Three tests in tests/replay_p2p_provision cover symmetric pair issuance without root-key disclosure, no durable writes, incarnation rotation, bad MAC/current- registration refusal, self/unknown-peer rejection, delayed-reply correlation and per-member request budgets. The native P2P Direct owner now requests these decisions before admitting a physical ENet connection, including process replacement.
